root_causes.name: Admin granting privileges to themselves (self-grant)
root_causes.description: A role was granted membership/privileges by itself (grantor = member). Self-granted privileges are a hallmark of privilege abuse by an insider who already holds elevated rights.
root_causes.resolution: Review the self-granted role membership. Revoke privileges that were not approved through change control, and require all grants to go through a separate approver (separation of duties).

expected.description: Role membership rows where the grantor is also the member

detect.postgresql: SELECT g.rolname AS grantor, m.rolname AS member, r.rolname AS granted_role FROM pg_auth_members am JOIN pg_roles g ON g.oid = am.grantor JOIN pg_roles m ON m.oid = am.member JOIN pg_roles r ON r.oid = am.roleid WHERE am.grantor = am.member ORDER BY m.rolname

root_causes.name: Excessive number of superusers
root_causes.description: More principals hold superuser/sysadmin than a least-privilege posture warrants. A large superuser population widens the insider-abuse blast radius and is hard to monitor.
root_causes.resolution: Review every superuser. Remove standing superuser from accounts that don't need it; prefer time-boxed elevation (break-glass) with auditing. Tune the acceptable count per environment.

expected.description: Superuser roles (alert when more than the per-customer threshold)

detect.postgresql: SELECT rolname, rolcanlogin FROM pg_roles WHERE rolsuper ORDER BY rolname

root_causes.name: Off-hours privileged sessions
root_causes.description: Superuser/admin sessions started outside business hours (before 07:00 or at/after 19:00 server time). Off-hours admin activity is a common insider-abuse indicator and should be paired with another signal before alerting.
root_causes.resolution: Correlate off-hours superuser sessions with change tickets / on-call schedules. Investigate any session with no corresponding approved activity. Tune the business-hours window per customer.

expected.description: Superuser sessions opened outside business hours

detect.postgresql: SELECT sa.usename, host(sa.client_addr) AS client_addr, sa.backend_start, sa.state FROM pg_stat_activity sa JOIN pg_roles r ON r.rolname = sa.usename WHERE r.rolsuper AND sa.backend_start IS NOT NULL AND (extract(hour FROM sa.backend_start) < 7 OR extract(hour FROM sa.backend_start) >= 19) ORDER BY sa.backend_start DESC

root_causes.name: Separation-of-duties violation
root_causes.description: A principal holds both sides of an operator-defined conflict pair (e.g., can both create payments and approve them). Requires the customer's SoD conflict matrix as an operator-supplied feed.
root_causes.resolution: Remove one side of each conflicting privilege pair, or introduce a compensating control (independent approval). Maintain the SoD conflict matrix per customer.

expected.description: Principals holding a conflicting privilege pair

root_causes.name: Privileged access to objects outside role baseline
root_causes.description: A DBA/privileged user read objects outside their per-principal expected-object baseline. Requires an audit trail (pgAudit / SQL Server Audit / Oracle Unified Audit) plus the per-principal baseline as operator feeds.
root_causes.resolution: Investigate access to objects outside the principal's baseline. Tighten object permissions; enable per-object auditing for sensitive tables. Warm the baseline before alerting.

expected.description: Audited object reads outside the principal baseline

root_causes.name: Pre-departure mass extraction
root_causes.description: Rows-read by a user spiked versus their personal baseline while they appear in the offboarding feed (resignation/notice). Requires per-user access stats + an HR/IDP offboarding feed as operator inputs.
root_causes.resolution: Freeze or closely monitor accounts in the offboarding window. Investigate the extraction (which tables, volume, destination). Tune the spike multiplier and baseline window per customer.

expected.description: Departing users whose read volume exceeds their baseline
